venues.name: Roberts Projects
venues.about: Roberts Projects is a Los Angeles gallery representing mid-career, established, and emerging artists working across drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, film, and performance. Founded in 1999 as Roberts & Tilton by Bennett Roberts, Julie Roberts, and Jack Tilton, the gallery occupied the Miracle Mile's 6150 Gallery Complex, then a converted coffee-roasting factory in Culver City, before taking its name Roberts Projects in 2018 following Tilton's passing. In 2023 the gallery relocated to a converted 1948 automobile showroom on South La Brea Avenue in Mid-Wilshire. The program emphasizes museum-quality, installation-based exhibitions and periodic historical surveys, spanning multiple generations and continents. The gallery also runs a publications division producing artist books and catalogues, and maintains a permanent site-specific niche installation by artist Betye Saar.

venues.name: Luis De Jesus Los Angeles
venues.about: Luis De Jesus Los Angeles is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2007 in San Diego by partners Luis De Jesus and Jay Wingate under the name Luis De Jesus Seminal Projects. The gallery relocated to Santa Monica in 2010, rebranding as Luis De Jesus Los Angeles, then moved to the Culver City Arts District in 2011, where it operated for a decade. Since spring 2021 it has occupied an expansive space on the edge of downtown Los Angeles's Arts District. The gallery represents a diverse roster of artists whose work engages personal, social, cultural, and aesthetic concerns, with many receiving major awards, biennial invitations, and museum acquisitions.

venues.name: Nicodim Gallery
venues.about: Nicodim Gallery is a contemporary art gallery led by owner Mihai Nicodim, with spaces in Los Angeles, New York, and Bucharest. Its program centers on painting and sculpture by an international, cross-generational roster of artists, including figures from Zimbabwe, South Africa, Romania, Spain, and the United States. The gallery has built a reputation for introducing artists such as Isabelle Albuquerque, Devin B. Johnson, Adrian Ghenie, and Moffat Takadiwa to wider audiences, later supported by major institutional exhibitions and biennials. Nicodim regularly participates in international art fairs including Frieze, Art Basel, and The Armory Show, and maintains an active exhibition schedule across its three locations, reflecting a program invested in figuration, materiality, and voices from outside traditional Western art centers.

venues.name: David Kordansky Gallery
venues.about: David Kordansky Gallery is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2003 in Los Angeles's Chinatown neighborhood as an incubator for emerging artists. It moved to Culver City in 2008 and now operates a 20,000-square-foot campus in Mid-City Los Angeles, alongside a 5,000-square-foot space in Chelsea, New York. The Los Angeles site comprises three exhibition spaces across two buildings with a courtyard, allowing simultaneous shows and programming that includes performance, film, and outdoor sculpture. The gallery represents artists working across all media, emphasizing individuality over a shared aesthetic, and situates its program within the history of postwar Los Angeles art while engaging global contemporary practice. It regularly participates in major international art fairs and produces exhibition catalogues and artist's books.

venues.name: Regen Projects
venues.about: Regen Projects is a contemporary art gallery on Santa Monica Boulevard in Los Angeles. The gallery represents an international roster of established and emerging artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, film, and installation. Its program has become known for supporting artists who engage with conceptual, social, and political concerns, spanning generations from pioneers of Conceptual and Minimal art to younger figures working in figuration and abstraction today. Regen Projects regularly organizes solo exhibitions for its artists in Los Angeles and participates in major international art fairs, while its artists are frequently included in biennials, museum surveys, and public commissions worldwide. The gallery also represents several artist estates, continuing the legacies of important late-twentieth-century figures.

venues.name: Perrotin
venues.about: Perrotin is an international contemporary art gallery founded in Paris in 1990 by Emmanuel Perrotin, then twenty-one years old. Over three decades the gallery has expanded to more than a dozen spaces across Europe, Asia and the United States, including Los Angeles. Its program is deliberately eclectic, spanning painting, sculpture, ceramics and new media, and bringing together long-represented artists alongside younger and emerging figures and several estates. The roster reflects a wide range of nationalities and generations, and the gallery is known for pairing gallery exhibitions with off-site museum projects, editions, a podcast, and public events.

venues.name: The Pit
venues.about: The Pit is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles founded in 2014 by artists Adam D. Miller and Devon Oder. It began as an artist-run, artist-curated project space in a former mechanics garage in Glendale before relocating, after a decade, to a larger complex in Atwater Village designed by JK & Co. The gallery represents and exhibits emerging, mid-career and established artists across generations, with a program grounded in dialogue with historical California art traditions, emphasizing material exploration, design, and counterculture influences. The Pit participates in major national and international art fairs and is a member of several art-dealer associations.

venues.name: Sprüth Magers
venues.about: Sprüth Magers is an international gallery for postwar and contemporary art, founded by Monika Sprüth in Cologne in 1983 and joined by Philomene Magers, whose own gallery merged with Sprüth's in 1998. Known for close, curatorially rigorous relationships with artists and museums, the gallery built its reputation on conceptual, photography-based and feminist-inflected practices, showing figures such as Rosemarie Trockel, Cindy Sherman, Barbara Kruger and John Baldessari from early on. In 2016 it opened its Los Angeles space on the Miracle Mile, its first US location, debuting with new works by Baldessari. The LA gallery continues the program's mix of longstanding conceptualists, mid-career figures and emerging voices across painting, sculpture, photography and installation.

venues.name: Matthew Marks Gallery
venues.about: Matthew Marks Gallery was founded in New York in 1991 and today represents thirty-five artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and printmaking. The gallery has grown to five exhibition spaces—three in New York and two in Los Angeles—totaling more than 18,000 square feet, and mounts between thirteen and fifteen exhibitions each year, often accompanied by original publications. Its program spans multiple generations of artists and a broad range of media, reflecting a long-standing commitment to both established and younger practitioners.

venues.name: Michael Kohn Gallery
venues.about: Michael Kohn Gallery was founded in 1985 by Michael Kohn, opening first on Robertson Boulevard in West Hollywood before relocating in 2014 to its current home on North Highland Avenue in Los Angeles. The gallery presents historically grounded exhibitions alongside a contemporary program, linking postwar West Coast movements such as Beat assemblage, Light and Space, and California Minimalism to newer generations of painters and sculptors. It represents senior West Coast figures including Lita Albuquerque and Sharon Ellis, oversees the estates of Bruce Conner, Wallace Berman, Joe Goode, and Martha Alf, and maintains a growing roster of emerging and mid-career artists working internationally, spanning painting, assemblage, and mixed-media practice with an emphasis on figuration, identity, and material experimentation.

venues.name: Megan Mulrooney
venues.about: Megan Mulrooney is a contemporary art gallery on Santa Monica Boulevard in Los Angeles, founded in 2024 by Megan Mulrooney, a lifelong Angeleno and former senior director at Nino Mier Gallery. The gallery represents emerging and mid-career artists from Los Angeles and abroad, staging solo exhibitions alongside artist-curated group presentations that encourage artists to participate in curatorial discourse. Its program blends a traditional commercial model with a collaborative, artist-forward ethos historically associated with the LA art scene, fostering cross-generational dialogue across two to three exhibitions per cycle. The gallery occupies a space formerly run by Nino Mier Gallery and has quickly built a presence on the national art fair circuit.

venues.name: Nazarian / Curcio
venues.about: Nazarian / Curcio is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles, owned by Shulamit Nazarian and Seth Curcio. Nazarian founded the gallery in Venice, CA in 2012, initially focusing on artists from the greater Middle East. Curcio joined in 2016, and together they broadened the program to emerging, mid-career, and established artists whose work engages social and political issues through personal narrative. In 2017 the gallery moved to a 6,000-square-foot, two-story building on La Brea Avenue in Hollywood, with two exhibition spaces, a library, offices, and viewing rooms. The gallery represents artists based in the U.S. and abroad, with an emphasis on those working in Los Angeles, and regularly participates in major national and international art fairs.

venues.name: Night Gallery
venues.about: Night Gallery is a contemporary art gallery based in the Arts District of Los Angeles, at 2050 Imperial Street. Led by owner Davida Nemeroff, the gallery represents an international roster of emerging and mid-career artists working across painting, sculpture, and installation. Its program includes solo and group exhibitions, publications, and an active presence at major international art fairs such as Frieze, Art Basel Miami Beach, The Armory Show, and NADA. Night Gallery artists have received extensive press coverage in outlets including The New York Times, Artforum, Frieze, and Hyperallergic, and its exhibitions frequently travel to museums and institutions worldwide.

venues.name: Pace Gallery
venues.about: Pace's Los Angeles gallery is the West Coast flagship of Pace Gallery, an international gallery founded by Arne Glimcher in Boston in 1960. Pace has had a presence in California for six decades and opened this dedicated LA space, on La Brea Avenue, in 2022. As part of Pace's global program, the Los Angeles gallery presents an intergenerational mix of contemporary and modern artists, connecting newer voices with long-represented figures and legacy estates. The gallery's program reflects Pace's broader emphasis on dialogue between contemporary practice and twentieth-century art, including strong historical ties to the Light and Space movement associated with Southern California.

venues.name: Lisson Gallery
venues.about: Lisson Gallery is an internationally established contemporary art gallery founded in 1967 by Nicholas Logsdail, with roots in Minimal and Conceptual art. Today it represents more than 70 artists spanning generations and geographies, from postwar figures like Carl Andre and Sol LeWitt to contemporary names such as Ai Weiwei, Marina Abramović and Hiroshi Sugimoto. Its Los Angeles space opened in 2023 in Hollywood's Sycamore District, occupying a standalone two-story building of over 8,000 square feet, with an inaugural exhibition of Carmen Herrera's Days of the Week series. The gallery also maintains spaces in London, New York and Shanghai, continuing its history of introducing international artists to new audiences.

venues.name: Louis Stern Fine Arts
venues.about: Louis Stern Fine Arts is a gallery in West Hollywood's Design District focused on Mid-Century West Coast Geometric Abstraction, representing the artists who defined California Hard Edge painting, including Lorser Feitelson, Helen Lundeberg and Karl Benjamin, alongside other Mid-Century abstractionists such as John McLaughlin, Frederick Hammersley and Roger Kuntz. The gallery also manages several artist estates, among them Mark Feldstein, Ynez Johnston, Matsumi Kanemitsu, Alfredo Ramos Martínez, Mimi Chen Ting, Doug Ohlson and Frederick Wight. Its contemporary roster includes painters, sculptors and photographers who extend this historic program. Beyond exhibitions, the gallery is active in the secondary market, with particular strength in Impressionist, Post-Impressionist, Modern and Latin American art, and oversees the catalogue raisonné project for Alfredo Ramos Martínez.

venues.name: Marc Selwyn Fine Art (Camden Downstairs Annex)
Tierra Del Sol Gallery
venues.about: Tierra del Sol Gallery is the exhibition space of the Tierra del Sol Foundation, a Los Angeles-area nonprofit founded in 1971 that supports artists with disabilities through studio space, career development, and materials. A dedicated gallery opened in West Hollywood in 2019 to expand the foundation's programming and connect its artists with a wider audience. The gallery organizes year-round exhibitions and events, frequently inviting guest curators such as Alison Saar, Darren Romanelli, and jill moniz. Its program centers on drawing, painting, ceramics, and textile work by self-taught and outsider artists, with pieces acquired by institutions including MoMA, the American Folk Art Museum, and El Museo del Barrio. Proceeds from sales support the artists and the broader foundation.

venues.name: David Zwirner
venues.about: David Zwirner is an international contemporary and postwar art gallery with locations in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris, and Hong Kong. It represents more than seventy artists and estates and is known for ambitious, cross-media exhibitions spanning painting, photography, sculpture, and installation, alongside active secondary-market dealing. The gallery was founded in 1993 in New York and expanded internationally over the following decades. Its Los Angeles presence debuted in 2023 with spaces in Melrose Hill, followed in 2024 by a standalone building designed, like all of the gallery's spaces, by Selldorf Architects. The Los Angeles gallery shares the program of the wider David Zwirner enterprise, presenting exhibitions by the gallery's international roster of established and emerging artists.

venues.name: Gagosian Beverly Hills
venues.about: Gagosian is a global gallery for modern and contemporary art founded by Larry Gagosian in Los Angeles in 1980. From that first space it has grown into a network of exhibition spaces across the United States, Europe, and Asia, designed by architects including Richard Meier, Jean Nouvel, and Selldorf Architects. The program pairs a roster of leading living artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and design with museum-quality historical exhibitions of twentieth-century masters. The gallery also runs a publishing arm producing catalogues raisonnés, monographs, and the Gagosian Quarterly magazine, and has developed initiatives supporting artists' estates and legacy planning alongside talks, screenings, and studio-visit programming.

venues.name: Timothy Hawkinson Gallery
venues.about: Timothy Hawkinson Gallery is a Los Angeles space on Beverly Boulevard that presents contemporary painting and drawing-based practices, largely through art-fair presentations such as NADA New York, NADA Miami, and Felix Art Fair. Its program pairs emerging and mid-career Los Angeles artists—among them Alise Spinella, Marc Pally, Mason Saltarrelli, and Samantha Yun Wall—with historically significant figures such as the Wiyot artist Rick Bartow and Mexico City-based Adrián S. Bará. The gallery emphasizes intuitive, process-driven abstraction, drawing, and works that explore the body, time, and cultural identity. It is a member of NADA and the Gallery Association Los Angeles (GALA).

venues.name: Vielmetter Los Angeles
venues.about: Vielmetter Los Angeles is a contemporary art gallery in the Arts District of downtown Los Angeles, located at 1700 S Santa Fe Avenue. It is owned and directed by Susanne Vielmetter and operates three exhibition spaces at that address. The gallery represents a multigenerational group of artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, video, and installation, including figures such as Nicole Eisenman, Arlene Shechet, Mickalene Thomas, Wangechi Mutu, Mary Kelly, and the estate of William Pope.L. Represented artists have participated in major international biennials, museum surveys, and art fairs, and have received sustained critical attention in publications including The New York Times, Artforum, The Guardian, and Artnet. The gallery's program spans several decades of contemporary practice, with a consistent focus on socially engaged, figurative, and materially inventive work by artists based in Los Angeles, New York, and internationally.

venues.name: Diane Rosenstein Gallery
venues.about: Diane Rosenstein Gallery is a contemporary fine art gallery founded in 2012 by Diane Rosenstein, located in the Hollywood neighborhood of Los Angeles. The gallery represents emerging, midcareer, and established artists working across a wide range of media, including painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, and ceramics. Its program has featured artists such as Eleanor Antin, Julian Stanczak, Amir Zaki, and Terran Last Gun, reflecting an interest in both historical and contemporary practices. The gallery participates regularly in major art fairs, including Independent, Untitled Art, and Art Basel Miami Beach, and its artists' work is frequently reviewed in national art publications.

venues.name: Good Mother Gallery
venues.about: Good Mother Gallery was founded in Oakland in 2014 and is now anchored in Los Angeles' West Adams district, while maintaining its original Oakland space. The gallery focuses on California's contemporary art scene, presenting monthly exhibitions of artists it describes as risk-takers, spanning emerging and established practices. Beyond its exhibition program, Good Mother Gallery curates offsite projects and public art initiatives, drawing on a decade of experience in civic art collaborations. It is a member of the New Art Dealers Alliance (NADA) and the Gallery Association Los Angeles (GALA), and works with artists nationally and internationally to build collector relationships and artist careers.

venues.name: Jeffrey Deitch
venues.about: Jeffrey Deitch is a contemporary art gallery founded by dealer, curator and writer Jeffrey Deitch, who opened its Los Angeles space in September 2018 after directing Deitch Projects in New York (1996–2010) and serving as director of MOCA Los Angeles. The gallery is known for ambitious thematic group shows such as People, Punch and Shattered Glass, alongside solo exhibitions with artists including Ai Weiwei, Judy Chicago, Urs Fischer, Robert Longo, Nari Ward and Rammellzee. Its program spans painting, sculpture, performance and street-art-influenced practices, continuing Deitch's long engagement with artists such as Keith Haring, Jean-Michel Basquiat and Jeff Koons. The gallery also maintains a New York space and participates actively in international art fairs.

venues.name: albertz benda
venues.about: Albertz benda is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2015, with its flagship space in Chelsea, New York, and a second location that opened in Los Angeles in 2021, presented within a domestic setting. The gallery's program centers on solo exhibitions of emerging and mid-career artists alongside thematic group shows, bringing together a global roster whose work engages cultural and social dialogues and questions of materiality across generations and disciplines. Albertz benda also undertakes historical research projects, revisiting the full careers of overlooked or historic figures and situating them within contemporary contexts. The gallery has supported institutional projects and acquisitions, with works by its artists held in numerous public collections worldwide.

venues.name: Musichead Gallery
venues.about: Musichead Gallery is a Los Angeles gallery devoted to fine-art music photography, founded in 1998 by Detroit-born music entrepreneur Sam Milgrom, who previously ran the record store Sam's Jams and the live venue The Magic Bag before relocating to the West Coast. Located on Sunset Boulevard in Hollywood, the gallery represents more than eighty music photographers and offers vintage and contemporary prints spanning decades of rock, pop, jazz, and soul history, alongside in-house custom framing and art-consultancy services. Its rotating exhibitions have focused on individual artists and eras, from Miles Davis and Joni Mitchell to Oasis and Madonna, often drawing on photographers' archives and estates.

venues.name: Tyler Park Presents
venues.about: Tyler Park Presents is a contemporary art gallery founded in September 2020 by Tyler Park, originally housed in a converted apartment in Los Angeles's Silver Lake neighborhood. The gallery represents and exhibits emerging and established artists working across painting, photography, sculpture, and mixed media, staging six to seven exhibitions a year, including solo and group presentations. It has built a track record of organizing artists' first solo exhibitions in Los Angeles, with nearly half of its solo shows marking such debuts. The gallery participates regularly in art fairs including NADA, Future Fair, Material Art Fair, Felix Art Fair, and Frieze Los Angeles, and is a member of the New Art Dealers Alliance. It is planning to relocate to the Melrose Hill neighborhood in September 2026.

venues.name: Hauser & Wirth Downtown Los Angeles
venues.about: Hauser & Wirth Downtown Los Angeles is the Los Angeles outpost of the international gallery founded in 1992 in Zurich by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser. The Los Angeles space opened in March 2016 in the Arts District, occupying the historic former Globe Mills flour-mill complex, restored in consultation with Selldorf Architects. The campus combines exhibition galleries with an open-air courtyard, garden and the Manuela restaurant, and hosts a robust learning and community-engagement program built around partnerships with local schools, universities and nonprofits. As part of the wider Hauser & Wirth program, the Los Angeles gallery presents historically minded surveys alongside contemporary exhibitions, drawing on the gallery's roster of more than ninety living artists and artist estates spanning painting, sculpture, photography and installation across generations and geographies.

venues.name: The Landing
venues.about: The Landing is a fine art gallery in Los Angeles specializing in historically significant twentieth-century postwar works, with particular attention to art made in California, alongside a program of contemporary artists. Operating from a 2,800-square-foot space on Jefferson Boulevard, the gallery presents a rotating schedule of solo, two-person, and thematic group exhibitions. It represents a roster that spans both historical and living artists, bridging mid-century West Coast art history with current practice. The gallery is led by owner Gerard O'Brien and participates regularly in major art fairs across the United States.

venues.name: Richard Heller Gallery
venues.about: Richard Heller Gallery is a contemporary art space in Santa Monica, California, run by director and owner Richard Heller with associate director Barry Belkin. Established in 1997, the gallery presents a program centered on figurative and narrative painting, drawing, ceramics, and photography by an international roster of emerging and mid-career artists. Known for supporting artists early in their careers—several of whom went on to significant critical attention—the gallery has built a reputation for eclectic, often humor-inflected exhibitions spanning painting, sculpture, and works on paper. Located at Bergamot Station, the gallery regularly participates in major art fairs and has been the subject of numerous press features on its artists in publications such as the Los Angeles Times, Juxtapoz, and Artillery.

venues.name: Wilding Cran Gallery
venues.about: Wilding Cran Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles, founded in 2014 by Naomi Wilding and Anthony Cran. Now located at 607 N Western Avenue, the gallery represents a roster of emerging and mid-career artists working across painting, sculpture, photography and mixed media, including Karon Davis, Fran Siegel, Ry Rocklen and Polly Borland. Its program has been featured at major international fairs such as Frieze Los Angeles, Frieze New York, Frieze London, The Armory Show, EXPO Chicago, FELIX Art Fair and NADA New York, and its exhibitions have drawn coverage from outlets including the Los Angeles Times, Artforum, The New York Times and The Guardian. The gallery is a member of the Gallery Association Los Angeles (GALA) and the New Art Dealers Alliance (NADA).

venues.name: Fahey/Klein Gallery
venues.about: Fahey/Klein Gallery is a Los Angeles photography gallery founded in 1986 by David Fahey and Randee Klein Devlin. Ken Devlin joined as co-owner in 1998; David Fahey has led the gallery since 2016. Located on North La Brea Avenue, the gallery specializes in 20th-century and contemporary fine art photography, with an inventory of more than 8,000 prints spanning portraiture, nudes, landscapes, still life, reportage and documentary work. Its exhibition program has featured photographers from Edward Weston and Man Ray to Herb Ritts and James Nachtwey, and the gallery mounts new two-person shows roughly every five weeks. Staff also curate touring exhibitions for museums and galleries abroad, contribute to photography publications, and maintain an active secondary-market and private-collection advisory practice.

venues.name: Art Share L.A.
venues.about: Art Share L.A. is a nonprofit arts organization in the Arts District of downtown Los Angeles, occupying a 30,000-square-foot building that combines 30 affordable artist lofts with exhibition and performance space. Its mission is to provide emerging artists equitable access and opportunity, connecting them to a supportive creative environment where they can live, work, develop, perform, and exhibit. The organization emphasizes diversity, equity, and inclusion, aiming to counter barriers faced by Black, Indigenous, People of Color, disabled, LGBTQ+, low-income, and other historically marginalized artists. It also advocates for fair, living wages for artists and staff, and works to connect artists with paid opportunities, from art sales to public art commissions.

venues.name: The Artists Gallery (TAG)
venues.about: The Artists Gallery (TAG) is an artist-founded, not-for-profit arts cooperative now based in the Miracle Mile district of Los Angeles. Established in Santa Monica in 1993, TAG is run and staffed by its member artists rather than commercial dealers. Its program centers on Southern Californian, national, and international artists working across media, with monthly solo and group exhibitions plus recurring juried shows such as Made in the USA, the L.A. Open, and the Shelley Lazarus Excellence in Watercolor Exhibition. The gallery also hosts artist talks, studio nights, and community events, reflecting its mission to support free exploration of media, technique, and content among its member artists.

venues.name: Cirrus Gallery
venues.about: Cirrus Gallery & Cirrus Editions Ltd. is a Los Angeles gallery, publisher, and print workshop founded by Jean Robert Milant in 1970. Originally based in Hollywood, it moved downtown to Alameda Street in 1979, helping shape the emerging Arts District, before relocating in 2015 to its current South Santa Fe Avenue space. Cirrus has long combined fine-art publishing with exhibition-making, working closely with generations of Los Angeles-based artists across painting, sculpture, installation, performance, video, and new media. Its program emphasizes original limited-edition prints produced in-house alongside gallery exhibitions, reflecting a sustained commitment to Southern California's postwar and contemporary art scenes.

venues.name: Charlie James Gallery
venues.about: Charlie James Gallery opened in 2008 in Los Angeles' Chinatown and has built a program centered on emerging and established artists with distinct, often political voices. The gallery works across painting, sculpture, textile, installation, and new media, with particular attention to marginalized perspectives and narratives touching on identity, race, gender, and broader socio-political concerns. Under gallery director Ever Velasquez, the program has become known for thoughtful, provocative curatorial approaches, including annual group exhibitions, and for close collaboration with museums and academics to help place artists' work within broader critical and historical conversations. The gallery now operates two adjoining spaces on historic Chung King Road.

venues.name: Nüart Gallery
venues.about: Nüart Gallery was established in Santa Fe at the start of the 21st century and has grown into a 3,000-square-foot, ten-room space on Canyon Road showing contemporary abstract and figurative art. Over more than two decades it has mounted upwards of 250 solo and group exhibitions, introducing many artists to the U.S. market and shipping worldwide. In 2023 the gallery expanded with a second 3,000-square-foot location at Bergamot Station in Santa Monica, extending its reach into the Los Angeles market. The program represents around 40 artists working locally and internationally, with works held in major museum collections such as MoMA, LACMA, the Getty, and the Tate Modern. The gallery also carries limited inventory from blue-chip artists.

venues.name: Patricia Sweetow Gallery
venues.about: Patricia Sweetow Gallery is a contemporary art gallery that opened in San Francisco in 1997 and relocated to Downtown Los Angeles in 2022, where it now operates from South Santa Fe Avenue. The gallery is led by principal Patricia Sweetow with associate director Christal Darling. Its program centers on artists working in non-traditional materials—textile, ceramic, fiber, and craft-based practices—that challenge institutional hierarchies between 'high' and 'low' art. Exhibiting artists often draw on craft traditions to interrogate colonial structures, personal identity, and cultural memory. The gallery has participated in numerous art fairs across the U.S. and Canada and represents a roster of emerging and mid-career artists working across sculpture, painting, ceramics, and fiber art.

venues.name: Parrasch Heijnen
venues.about: Parrasch heijnen is a gallery in the Boyle Heights neighborhood of Los Angeles. Its program brings together postwar Los Angeles Light and Space and geometric abstraction, work by artists associated with the historic Brockman Gallery and the Black Arts Council, and a roster of contemporary painters and sculptors working in abstraction and assemblage. The gallery represents several artist estates, including those of Peter Alexander, Tony DeLap, Forrest Bess, Marcia Hafif and Alonzo Davis, alongside living artists such as Anne Appleby, Edith Baumann, Alteronce Gumby, Xylor Jane, Kristy Luck, Mildred Howard and Christine Howard Sandoval. The gallery participates regularly in international art fairs, including Frieze, Art Basel Miami Beach, NADA, Independent and the Dallas Art/Invitational fairs, and has organized historical group presentations such as 'Brockman Days' surveying the artists of the pioneering Black-owned Brockman Gallery.

venues.name: Peter Fetterman Gallery
venues.about: Peter Fetterman Gallery is a Santa Monica photography gallery founded by Peter Fetterman, a London-born collector and former filmmaker who opened his first gallery in 1988 and became one of the original tenants of Bergamot Station when it opened in 1994. The gallery holds one of the largest inventories of classic twentieth-century photography in the United States, with particular depth in humanist photography. Its holdings include work by figures such as Henri Cartier-Bresson, Sebastião Salgado, Steve McCurry, Ansel Adams, Paul Caponigro, Willy Ronis, Michael Kenna, André Kertész, Manuel Alvarez Bravo, Lillian Bassman, Pentti Sammallahti, Sarah Moon and Jeffrey Conley. The gallery presents this work in an intimate, salon-style setting intended to promote appreciation of the photographic medium.

venues.name: Yiwei Gallery
venues.about: Yiwei Gallery was founded in Los Angeles in 2019 by curator and collector Yiwei Lu, initially operating an artist-in-residence program out of a house before formally opening in Venice Beach in 2021. The gallery has focused on cultural exchange, consistently centering artists from East Asia and its diaspora alongside American and European artists working in painting, installation, textile and photography. After closing its Venice Beach space in 2024, Yiwei Gallery opened a 5,000-square-foot venue in Wuhan the same year, with a new Los Angeles location planned for 2025. The gallery also co-presents the C Art Festival in Wuhan and participates widely in international art fairs.

venues.name: Marshall Gallery
venues.about: Marshall Gallery is a Santa Monica photography gallery founded in 2018 by Douglas Marshall and opened to the public in 2021 at Bergamot Station Arts Center. The program centers on contemporary and 20th-century lens-based art, with particular attention to experimental processes, printmaking craft and conceptual approaches to photography and video. In recent years the roster has increasingly explored the intersection of photographic practice with painting and sculpture. Alongside a regular schedule of exhibitions, the gallery hosts artist conversations and community events and participates in art fairs internationally, positioning itself within ongoing conversations about photography's evolving role in contemporary art and collective memory.

venues.name: Make Room
venues.about: Make Room is a contemporary art gallery in Hollywood, Los Angeles, founded in 2018 by collector and curator Emilia Yin. It occupies interconnected exhibition spaces with an outdoor courtyard and garden. The program centers on artists exploring cultural identity, conceptual practice and global perspectives, often ahead of institutional recognition, with a stated commitment to female artists, artists of color and voices working outside established centers. Shaped by Yin's position between Los Angeles and Asia, the gallery has introduced emerging artists and reframed established ones, including Terence Koh, Sun Woo, Andrew Sendor, Guimi You, Yeni Mao, Tuan Vu, Xin Liu and Jacopo Pagin. Works by its artists have entered major public collections including LACMA, the Hammer Museum and the Institute of Contemporary Art Miami.

venues.name: Château Shatto
venues.about: Château Shatto is a contemporary art gallery based in Los Angeles that represents an international group of artists working across painting, sculpture, video, and installation. Its roster includes Aria Dean, Fiona Connor, Van Hanos, Helen Johnson, C.B. Evans, Cécile B. Evans, and the late Jacqueline de Jong, alongside a growing list of emerging names, with photographer John Divola joining the program in 2026. The gallery frequently presents artists' work at international institutions such as the Hammer Museum, Renaissance Society, ICA London, and Serralves Museum, and participates in art fairs including Art Basel and FIAC/OFFICIELLE. Its exhibitions and programming, including screenings and curated group shows, reflect an interest in conceptually driven, research-based practices spanning painting, sculpture, moving image, and site-specific installation.

venues.name: Nonaka-Hill
venues.about: Nonaka-Hill is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles founded in 2018 by Rodney and Taka Nonaka-Hill, with a second space in Kyoto, Japan. The program centers on modern and contemporary Japanese art, presenting many artists for the first time on the West Coast, spanning painting, ceramics, sculpture, and photography from postwar and contemporary Japan alongside a smaller group of international artists. Located in Hollywood near the intersection of Melrose and Highland, the gallery sits among a cluster of established Los Angeles galleries. Nonaka-Hill represents the estate of Yōga painter Zenzaburo Kojima and has built a program bridging Japanese art history with contemporary practice, participating regularly in international art fairs including Frieze, Art Basel, and Art Collaboration Kyoto.

venues.name: Feia
venues.about: Feia is a Los Angeles gallery founded by husband-duo Thomas Martinez Pilnik and Jake Cavallo. The name, Portuguese for "ugly," reflects a program built around curiosity, humor, and unconventional beauty rather than conventional polish. Pilnik, an artist and educator, and Cavallo, a designer with an architecture background, run Feia as a hybrid of exhibitions, events, dinners, and workshops emphasizing community and food alongside visual art. The gallery represents a small roster of emerging painters, sculptors, and mixed-media artists exploring queer identity, memory, and domestic space, and is especially active on the art fair circuit across Los Angeles, New York, Miami, and Chicago. It has also built a new gallery space in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles.

venues.name: Stroll Garden
venues.about: Stroll Garden is a Los Angeles gallery representing a roster of emerging and mid-career artists working primarily in ceramics and sculptural design, many with ties to Korean or Korean American heritage. The program spans hand-built stoneware, thrown vessels, and functional design objects, often presented in gallery exhibitions and at design fairs such as Design Miami. The gallery operates two Los Angeles spaces, one in the Hollywood Hills and one on Beverly Boulevard, and has built a reputation for showing artists whose work bridges fine art and design.

venues.name: Armory Center for the Arts
venues.about: Founded in 1989, Armory Center for the Arts is a nonprofit visual arts organization based in a historic 1932 California National Guard Armory building in Old Pasadena. It operates as a hybrid museum and art school, presenting contemporary art exhibitions alongside artist-led education programs for children, teens, and adults. Its roots trace back to the Pasadena Art Institute's Junior Museum program (1922), later evolving through the Pasadena Art Museum's Children's Art Workshop and the Pasadena Art Workshops before becoming the Armory in 1989. The organization emphasizes socially engaged, often BIPOC-centered contemporary art and free community-based art education, serving over 18,000 people annually across Pasadena and Los Angeles County, with particular focus on under-resourced neighborhoods and system-impacted communities.

venues.name: Track 16
venues.about: Track 16 is a Los Angeles gallery with two exhibition spaces, one in East Hollywood and one downtown in the historic Bendix Building. Sean Meredith serves as director. The program centers on a small roster of California-based and international artists working across painting, ceramics, sculpture, and installation, often engaging social and political themes—from feminist critiques of domestic craft (Elyse Pignolet) to politically charged painting (Sandow Birk, Robbie Conal) and reworked found ceramics (Debra Broz). The gallery also represents the estates of Pedro Álvarez and Simone Gad, and has shown Latin American collectives such as Mondongo. Track 16 participates in art fairs, publishes artist books under its Pinspot imprint, and has placed artists' work in institutions including LACMA, SFMOMA, and the Getty.

venues.name: Philip Martin Gallery
venues.about: Philip Martin Gallery is a contemporary art gallery based in Los Angeles that presents innovative, experimental and ambitious artworks in all media, both at its own space and at art fairs in the United States and abroad. In January 2023 the gallery moved into a new 4,000-square-foot location at 3342 Verdugo Road in Los Angeles. The gallery represents a roster of artists working across painting, photography, video, sculpture and textile, including figures such as Ericka Beckman, Kwame Brathwaite, Brian Bress and Carl Cheng, alongside a group of emerging and mid-career painters and sculptors. The gallery has a history that traces back to its earlier incarnation as Cherry and Martin.

venues.name: Gallery at REDCAT
venues.about: REDCAT (the Roy and Edna Disney CalArts Theater) is CalArts' downtown Los Angeles center for contemporary visual and performing arts, opened in November 2003 inside the Walt Disney Concert Hall complex designed by Frank Gehry. Initiated by Roy E. Disney as a gift from the Walt Disney Company and matched by Roy and Patty Disney, it houses a 250-seat black-box theater, a 3,000-square-foot gallery, and a lounge. Through performances, exhibitions, screenings, and literary events, REDCAT presents experimental and cutting-edge work by Los Angeles-based and international artists, extending CalArts' mission of experimentation, discovery, and civic discourse to a professional venue in the city's downtown cultural corridor.

venues.name: NOON Projects
venues.about: NOON Projects is a contemporary art gallery in Chinatown, Los Angeles, founded by Ryan Noon in 2022. The program presents emerging and historical artists working across painting, sculpture, performance, craft, and sound, with a focus on spirituality, eroticism, the natural world, queerness, and social practice. The gallery is known for close, collaborative relationships with its artists and an interdisciplinary curatorial approach that pairs exhibitions with a regular schedule of community programming, including concerts, lectures, dinners, workshops, salons, and performances. Noon brings a background in fashion and creative direction, having worked with Alexander McQueen and Henrik Vibskov and built a design studio and think tank at Nike, which informs the gallery's artist-centered, experimental sensibility and emphasis on long-term collaboration and dialogue between artists and audiences.

venues.name: Wonzimer
venues.about: Wönzimer is an independent gallery in Lincoln Heights, Los Angeles, founded by Swiss artist Alaïa Parhizi and American entrepreneur Aidan Nelson. Its German name, meaning "living room," reflects the founders' aim to create an intimate, home-like exhibition space rather than a conventional white-box gallery. The gallery represents thirteen artists working across painting, sculpture, and mixed media, and presents both solo shows and thematic group exhibitions that bring together established and emerging voices, including international projects. Beyond exhibitions, Wönzimer runs W.A.R.P., an artist residency program with on-site studios, and hosts artist talks, poetry readings, music, film screenings, and other cross-disciplinary programming. The space includes a hidden bookshelf leading to a lounge, continuing the gallery's living-room concept. Wönzimer has operated from earlier locations in Koreatown and downtown Los Angeles before settling in its current Lincoln Heights space.

venues.name: Gabba Gallery
venues.about: Gabba Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles that has been open since 2012, showing work by emerging and established artists from around the world with a strong emphasis on street art, graffiti-rooted practice, and mixed-media painting. Founded by Jason Ostro, who named the space after his late father's nickname for him, the gallery spent eleven years in Historic Filipinotown on Beverly Blvd before relocating to 235 S. Broadway in Downtown Los Angeles. Beyond its exhibition program, Gabba runs the Gabba Alley Project, bringing murals and public art into surrounding neighborhoods to foster community engagement.

venues.name: 18th Street Arts Center
venues.about: 18th Street Arts Center is a nonprofit artist residency and public-programs organization in Santa Monica, California, founded in 1988 by Susanna Bixby Dakin and Linda Frye Burnham out of a 1970s-80s community of feminist and performance artists that included Judy Chicago and Barbara T. Smith. Now one of the largest artist-residency programs in Southern California, it hosts local, national, and international artists for live/work studio stays, alongside organizations-in-residence such as Highways Performance Space. Its program blends exhibitions and public events in the Atrium Gallery and Artist's Hearth with community-engagement initiatives like Culture Mapping 90404, reflecting a long-standing commitment to socially engaged, research-driven contemporary art practice.

venues.name: Harkawik
venues.about: Harkawik is a contemporary art gallery founded by curator and artist Peter Harkawik. The gallery grew out of large survey exhibitions Harkawik organized at guest venues through the 2010s before opening a permanent space in Los Angeles in 2018. It expanded to New York's Lower East Side in 2020, later moving into a larger Tribeca location in 2024. The gallery represents fifteen artists with a strong international focus, presenting work across painting, sculpture, and other media, alongside a program of exhibited artists shown in group shows but not formally represented.

venues.name: Thinkspace Projects
venues.about: Thinkspace Projects is a Los Angeles gallery in the West Adams District, founded in 2005 by Andrew Hosner and L. Croskey. Since its start the gallery has built an international reputation as a leading voice for the New Contemporary Art Movement, a lowbrow-descended, figurative and pop-culture-inflected strain of art that emerged on the West Coast in the 1990s. Thinkspace represents artists ranging from emerging to established, and has expanded beyond its own space to curate exhibitions with museums and partner galleries in cities such as Berlin, Hong Kong, London, New York, Detroit, Chicago and Honolulu. It also produces murals worldwide and works with organizations like POW! WOW! and RAD Napa. The gallery describes itself as artist-focused, family-run, and committed to bridging street-level and institutional art contexts.

venues.name: Serious Topics
venues.about: Serious Topics is a small artist-run gallery in Inglewood, California, founded by artists Kristin Calabrese and Joshua Aster. The space operates informally, showing and selling works on paper and other modestly scaled pieces through its flatfiles and inventory, viewable by appointment. Its program brings together a wide roster of contemporary artists working in graphite, ink, watercolor, and collage, emphasizing intimate, works-on-paper practices over large-scale production. The gallery periodically mounts solo exhibitions, including a planned show by Susanna Coffey. Visits are by appointment, reflecting its low-key, artist-driven approach to running a commercial exhibition space.

venues.name: The Hive Gallery
venues.about: The Hive Gallery and Studios is a gallery and working-artist complex on Los Angeles' Downtown Art Walk, founded in Spring 2005 by Nathan Cartwright. It combines two exhibition galleries with about 25 working artist studios and an artist-made goods store. The program centers on neo-pop illustration and craft-driven, affordable work, with monthly opening shows featuring five spotlighted artists alongside large group exhibitions, live painting, and performance. Operating on low or no commission, the gallery emphasizes accessibility for new collectors while also offering higher-priced work from established artists. Beyond sales, it functions as a community hub hosting yoga, figure drawing, film screenings, and fundraising events, positioning itself as a long-running fixture of the Downtown LA art scene.

venues.name: Ysasi
venues.about: Casa Ysasi is a studio and gallery in Los Angeles founded by brothers Iñigo and Pato Ysasi, built around a shared sense of hermandad, or brotherhood, rooted in family and craft. The space is divided between a gallery for exhibiting prints and curated work and a working studio and showroom where light-based objects and prototypes are developed. Ysasi Gallery operates as a rotating, two-month exhibition and installation platform, working with local and international artists whose practices sit between art, design, and craft, with an emphasis on process-driven, site-specific work. The studio side, Studio Ysasi, focuses on light as a medium, producing objects and installations meant to evoke presence and calm.

venues.name: Commonwealth and Council
venues.about: Commonwealth and Council is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2010, originally operating from a one-bedroom apartment at the intersection of Commonwealth Avenue and Council Street before moving to its current space on West 7th Street. The gallery describes itself as a community, platform, and laboratory for ambitious, radical art, prioritizing minoritarian voices and pushing back against the art world's winner-take-all star system. Its program spans painting, sculpture, video, and performance, extending into public and educational initiatives such as the Commonwealth and Council Summer School and the Council Fund, which supports artists' health insurance and emergency needs. The gallery has built a reputation for championing experimental, socially engaged practices and regularly participates in major international fairs including Frieze, Art Basel, and Condo.

venues.name: Corey Helford Gallery
venues.about: Corey Helford Gallery (CHG) was founded in 2006 by Jan Corey Helford and her husband, television producer Bruce Helford. The gallery focuses on New Contemporary art, encompassing New Figurative Art, Pop Surrealism, Neo Pop, Graffiti and Street Art, and Post-Graffiti, representing a diverse roster of international artists ranging from emerging to established names. After nine years in Culver City, CHG relocated in December 2015 to a 12,000-square-foot building in Downtown Los Angeles, where it now operates three separate gallery spaces hosting individual and group exhibitions roughly every six weeks. The gallery has also exhibited at major art fairs and partnered with international institutions such as Bristol's City Museum & Art Gallery for a transatlantic exhibition in 2010.

venues.name: Band of Vices
venues.about: Band of Vices is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2015 by Terrell Tilford, who began it as a downtown pop-up before opening a permanent space in West Adams and later relocating to the Arts District. The gallery describes itself as growing from an artistic collaborative into an internationally recognized platform, with a stated mission of inclusion and support for artists who have historically been overlooked, including Black, brown, queer, and differently abled voices. Its program centers on emerging and mid-career contemporary artists with strong individual visions, and the gallery has built an international following through exhibitions, art fairs, and press coverage over the past decade.

venues.name: Los Angeles Municipal Art Gallery (LAMAG)
venues.about: Founded in 1954 within Barnsdall Art Park, the Los Angeles Municipal Art Gallery is the longest continuously running institution in Los Angeles devoted solely to exhibiting art. Operated by the city's Department of Cultural Affairs, it grew out of the city-led All City Outdoor Art Festivals and Kenneth Ross's vision for decentralized civic arts programming. The gallery focuses on artists connected to Los Angeles, with particular attention to underrepresented and emerging voices, alongside mid-career and established practitioners. Past exhibitors who later gained wider recognition include Carlos Almaraz, John Baldessari, Vija Celmins, David Hammons, Barbara Kruger, Kerry James Marshall, and Ed Ruscha. Admission and programs are free, and the gallery does not maintain a permanent collection.

venues.name: ROSEGALLERY
venues.about: ROSEGALLERY is a Los Angeles-area gallery founded in 1991 by Rose Shoshana at the Bergamot Station Arts Center in Santa Monica. The program centers on modern and contemporary photography, spanning works that draw on the medium's history as well as contemporary photo-based art. Shoshana, who trained at Art Center College of Design and worked in editorial photography before opening the gallery, has built relationships with artists such as William Eggleston, Bruce Davidson, and Graciela Iturbide, and has collaborated with institutions including the Getty Museum and Tate Modern. The gallery represents a roster of established and emerging photographers and lens-based artists, and regularly presents work at international art fairs including Paris Photo and Photo London.

venues.name: Weinstein Gallery
venues.about: Weinstein Gallery was founded in San Francisco in 1992 by Rowland Weinstein, with a focus on non-objective and surrealist art spanning pre-war Europe through the New York School and Abstract Expressionism. The gallery represents the estates of Rudolf Bauer and Juanita Guccione, and is known for championing women of the surrealist movement, including Leonor Fini, Leonora Carrington, Kay Sage, Stella Snead, Remedios Varo and Dorothea Tanning. It has also worked to revive attention to understudied artists such as Enrico Donati, Jimmy Ernst, Gordon Onslow Ford, Gerome Kamrowski and Kurt Seligmann through exhibitions, publications and museum loans. In Spring 2026 the gallery plans to open a project space in Los Angeles devoted to contemporary art, performance and multidisciplinary programming, extending its historical program into a dialogue with the present day.

venues.name: Chris Sharp Gallery
venues.about: Chris Sharp Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles, founded in January 2021 by writer and curator Chris Sharp, co-founder of the Mexico City project space Lulu. The program mixes emerging, mid-career, and historically overlooked artists, with a core group based in Los Angeles alongside artists working on the East Coast, in the UK, and in Europe. The gallery favors fully integrated practices in which ideas, politics, and materials are inseparable, giving weight to personal, idiosyncratic sensibilities, humor, and craft, presented with careful spatial attention. Chris Sharp serves as owner and director, supported by a small staff handling operations and exhibitions. The gallery is located on Santa Monica Boulevard and participates regularly in international art fairs.

venues.name: Bel Ami
venues.about: Bel Ami is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles, founded in the summer of 2016 by Naoki Sutter-Shudo and Sabrina Tarasoff. The gallery operates from a space inside the Asian Center on N. Hill Street in Chinatown. Its program centers on emerging and mid-career artists working across painting, sculpture, ceramics, and mixed media, with a roster spanning Los Angeles, Europe, and Japan. Bel Ami has built a reputation for adventurous, often narrative or satirical bodies of work, exhibiting artists such as Guillaume Dénervaud, Olivia Hill, Ben Sakoguchi, and Soshiro Matsubara. The gallery is a regular exhibitor at international art fairs, including Frieze, Liste, FIAC, Paris Internationale, miart, and the Dallas Invitational, and its exhibitions have been reviewed in numerous art publications.

venues.name: Roberts Projects LA
venues.about: Roberts Projects is a Los Angeles gallery representing mid-career and established artists alongside emerging talents from multiple generations and continents. Founded in 1999 as Roberts & Tilton by Bennett Roberts, Julie Roberts and Jack Tilton, the gallery renamed itself Roberts Projects in 2018 after Tilton's death. It has occupied three homes in Los Angeles: the Miracle Mile's 6150 complex, a converted coffee-roasting factory in Culver City, and since 2023 a restored 1948 automobile showroom on La Brea Avenue. The program favors museum-quality, installation-based exhibitions across drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, film and performance, periodically staging historical survey shows, and includes a publishing division producing artist monographs and catalogues.

venues.name: Keystone Art Space
venues.about: Keystone Art Space is a large working-artist complex in the Lincoln Heights/Cypress Park area of Los Angeles, housing more than fifty individual studios for painters, illustrators, sculptors, photographers, jewelers and designers. Within the warehouse, Keystone Gallery mounts rotating group and solo exhibitions and the space regularly opens to the public for a biannual Open Studios event, giving visitors direct access to tenant studios alongside curated shows. Past programming has included group exhibitions built around music, writing, photography and international artist exchanges, often organized by the resident community or visiting curators. The facility is led by Director Melanie Mandl, with Mark Harvey serving as Keystone Gallery Co-Director. Keystone functions less as a commercial gallery than as a hybrid studio building and public exhibition venue supporting a broad, multidisciplinary Los Angeles art community.

venues.name: The Broad
venues.about: The Broad is a contemporary art museum on Grand Avenue in downtown Los Angeles, founded in 2015 by philanthropists Eli and Edythe Broad as a gift to the city. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Gensler, its 120,000-square-foot 'veil-and-vault' building offers free general admission and houses over 2,000 postwar and contemporary works by nearly 200 artists, including Basquiat, Warhol, Koons, Kusama, Ruscha, and Kruger. The museum is also headquarters to the Broad Art Foundation's worldwide lending library, active since 1984. Under founding director Joanne Heyler, its program emphasizes rotating temporary exhibitions, monographic surveys, and public programming often centered on social justice themes, drawing over 900,000 visitors annually.

venues.name: Diversions Fine Arts
venues.about: Diversions Fine Arts is a membership gallery in Manhattan Beach, California, founded by arts writer and curator Genie Davis. It exhibits a wide range of contemporary artists from the greater Los Angeles area and beyond, working across mixed media, oil, acrylic, sculpture, and photography. Each month three artists are curated into a solo-style rotation, while group shows bring together artists from all membership tiers. The gallery operates on a low, 10% commission structure and also publishes the online magazine DiversionsLA.com, covering Southern California exhibitions since 2016. Its roster spans emerging and established artists working in painting, collage, neon, sculpture, and photography, reflecting a broad, inclusive approach to contemporary Southern California art.

venues.name: L.A. Louver
venues.about: L.A. Louver is a contemporary art gallery in Venice, California, founded in 1975 by Peter and Elizabeth Goulds. It opened to the public on North Venice Boulevard in 1976 with a mission to place Southern California artists in an international context while bringing global artists to Los Angeles audiences. Over five decades the gallery has represented a roster of established postwar and contemporary painters and sculptors, mounting hundreds of exhibitions and building an extensive archive documenting its history and artists' records. Its program spans painting, sculpture, assemblage, ceramics, and works on paper, with a strong emphasis on figuration, abstraction, and cross-generational dialogue between Los Angeles and international artists.

venues.name: Junior High
venues.about: Junior High is a multi-purpose art gallery, event space, and artist sanctuary in Glendale, California, founded by Faye Orlove. It describes itself as a community-driven venue dedicated to arts expression and arts education for people of all ages and backgrounds. Programming spans gallery shows, music events, workshops, panels, and editorial projects, with a particular focus on supporting marginalized and emerging artists, including beginners, women, queer and nonbinary artists, and artists of color. The space, which holds over 80 people, emphasizes radical empathy, accessibility, and safety as guiding values, positioning itself as an alternative to traditional, exclusionary art-world spaces.

venues.name: OXY Arts (Occidental College)
venues.about: OXY ARTS is the public arts center of Occidental College, located on York Boulevard in the Highland Park area of Los Angeles. It presents free exhibitions, performances, artist residencies (including the Wanlass Artist-in-Residence program), and workshops spanning film, visual art, performance, writing, and music. The program emphasizes projects led by Black, Indigenous, and people-of-color artists and organizers, and work that engages social and political issues. It also serves as a gateway to Occidental College's arts departments, offering hands-on internship and teaching opportunities for students, especially BIPOC and first-generation students, while building relationships with the wider Los Angeles arts community.

venues.name: Hammer Museum
venues.about: The Hammer Museum is a UCLA-affiliated contemporary art museum in Westwood, Los Angeles, founded by Armand Hammer and opened in November 1990. Since a 1994 partnership agreement, it has been operated by UCLA, absorbing the collections of the Wight Art Gallery and the Grunwald Center for the Graphic Arts as well as the Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden. Directors have included Henry Hopkins, Ann Philbin (1999–2024), and current director Zoë Ryan (from 2025). The museum is known for its Made in L.A. biennial, the ongoing Hammer Projects series, and an active calendar of lectures, film, and public programs. Admission is free.

venues.name: Aabee Bleue Project
venues.about: Aabee Bleue Project is a contemporary art space in Downtown Los Angeles that builds connections among cultures, communities, and contemporary artistic practices. Through exhibitions, conversations, and public programs, the gallery introduces contemporary artists from Iran, the Middle East, and beyond to new audiences and contexts. It was founded by Sabrina Younesi and Narges Hamzianpour, and developed alongside Niloufar Binafard, who serves as Artist Liaison and Art Advisor. The program is driven by curiosity, collaboration, and a desire to create dialogue between artists, ideas, and communities, using art as a means to build cross-cultural dialogue, challenge perspectives, and create spaces for discovery.

venues.name: Avenue 50 Studio
venues.about: Avenue 50 Studio is a nonprofit arts presentation organization in the Highland Park neighborhood of Northeast Los Angeles. Founded in 2000 by Kathy Gallegos, who continues to serve as its Founding Executive and Artistic Director, the space describes its mission as bridging cultures through content-driven visual art grounded in Latina/o culture and the Northeast LA community. The program mixes exhibitions of emerging and established artists with literary programming, including a long-running poetry series, workshops, and community projects such as mural restoration. Governed by a volunteer board of directors alongside its staff, the studio positions itself as a destination gallery for socially engaged, culturally rooted contemporary art.

venues.name: Royale Projects
venues.about: Royale Projects is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2008, dedicated to the history and ongoing development of abstraction in painting and sculpture, alongside artists whose work is rooted in Conceptualism. The gallery has presented debut exhibitions of artists such as Helen Pashgian, associated with the California Light & Space movement, and the last new works by Dennis Oppenheim. It has organized site-responsive desert projects in Joshua Tree, including collaborations with Andrea Zittel and Phillip K. Smith III. Its downtown Los Angeles Arts District space opened in 2015. The gallery participated in The Getty's Pacific Standard Time: LA/LA and represents the estate of Clinton Hill, contributing to renewed critical interest in his abstract paintings from the New York School.

venues.name: Billis/Williams Gallery
venues.about: Billis/Williams Gallery is a painting-focused gallery in the Culver City Arts District of Los Angeles, led by partner Tressa Williams. The program is technique-driven, spanning figurative, abstract, and still-life painting by a roster of California-based and national artists working primarily in oil and mixed media. Recurring themes include California landscapes and cityscapes, portraiture, domestic and still-life subjects, and meditative or abstract explorations of memory and place. The gallery participates regularly in national art fairs, including the Seattle Art Fair, San Francisco Art Fair, SCOPE Miami Beach, Intersect Palm Springs, and Palm Springs Modernism, and its artists are frequently covered in art press, interviews, and podcasts. The gallery describes itself as woman-owned.

venues.name: la BEAST gallery
venues.about: la BEAST gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles, founded in April 2022 by Roxana Eslamieh and Zack Christensen. Located at the corner of Cypress and Thorpe Avenues, the gallery's program centers on emerging and mid-career artists, with an emphasis on themes of mythology, naturalism, and the occult. Beyond its exhibition program, la BEAST participates annually in art fairs including NADA New York, NADA Miami, and Felix Art Fair, presenting group and solo showcases of its represented artists.

venues.name: Clockshop at Los Angeles State Historic Park
venues.about: Clockshop is a nonprofit arts organization based in the Elysian Valley/Frogtown neighborhood of Los Angeles, founded in 2004 by filmmaker Julia Meltzer. Rather than running a conventional exhibition space, it commissions artists to create site-specific, experimental projects on public land, especially along the LA River at the Bowtie Parcel and at Los Angeles State Historic Park, in long-term partnership with California State Parks. Its program combines artist commissions, publications, and public programming with environmental and community advocacy, focusing on equitable green space, local history, and the relationship between artists, communities, and public lands throughout the LA River watershed.

venues.name: Del Vaz Projects
venues.about: Del Vaz Projects is a nonprofit art space based in Los Angeles, founded in 2014 by Jay Ezra Nayssan in a home-turned-artists space in Santa Monica and accredited as a 501(c)(3) in 2021. The organization mounts exhibitions, produces publications, and stages performance and moving-image programs, often in partnership with museums, foundations, and other Los Angeles institutions. It positions itself as an incubator for artists, archives, and estates, pairing curatorial projects with a research collective and independent press that produce artist books and exhibition catalogs. Its program brings together artists across generations and geographies, with particular attention to underrepresented estates and archives and collaborations across the city's cultural institutions.

venues.name: Currency Exchange
venues.about: Currency Exchange (CXLA) is a Los Angeles gallery and community arts space that pairs its exhibition schedule with social-practice programming. Rather than functioning as a conventional white-box gallery, it uses its ground-floor space—situated within affordable housing along the West Washington corridor in Mid-City—as a gathering point for artists, residents, and neighbors. Alongside rotating exhibitions, CXLA runs Community Feeds tied to each show's closing, karaoke nights during exhibitions, artist talks, workshops, and a Beauty Salon series developed with Transformation Arts and the Agape Artist Residency. It also produces a neighborhood zine documenting Mid-City businesses and stories, and invites residents to create collaborative lobby artworks. The organization frames its programming as an investment in the surrounding community's social fabric.

venues.name: induction gallery
venues.about: induction gallery is a Los Angeles gallery founded and directed by artist and curator John Zinonos. Located at 672 S. La Fayette Park Place in the city's Westlake area, the space works by appointment and presents a roster of emerging and mid-career artists working across painting, sculpture, ceramics, photography, collage, and new media. The program reflects Zinonos's own multidisciplinary curatorial interests, bringing together Los Angeles-based and out-of-state artists whose practices engage material experimentation, personal narrative, and technology-driven or ecological themes.

venues.name: H Foundation for the Arts
venues.about: H Foundation for the Arts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit arts platform based in San Marino, California, founded in 2025 by Tina He, growing out of the earlier Cultural Foundations of Zhendai He (USA). The organization continues a legacy of cultural research and international exchange inspired by scholar and educator Zhendai He. Through exhibitions, residencies, and public programs, it supports contemporary artists from Asia and its diaspora, fostering dialogue between tradition and contemporary expression across cultures and generations. Its programming is complemented by Be An Culture, a related media and storytelling platform connecting global Chinese-speaking communities through cultural dialogue and collaborative projects.

venues.name: Getty Center
venues.about: The Getty Center is one of two Los Angeles-area sites operated by the J. Paul Getty Trust, a cultural organization founded on the legacy of businessman and art collector J. Paul Getty. Located in Brentwood, the Center presents European art from the Middle Ages to today amid modern architecture and gardens with views over Los Angeles. It is one of the Trust's four programs, alongside the Getty Research Institute, Getty Conservation Institute, and Getty Foundation. The Trust's second museum site, the Getty Villa, focuses on ancient Greek and Roman antiquities in Pacific Palisades. Admission to both locations is free with a timed-entry reservation.

venues.name: La Luz de Jesus Gallery
venues.about: La Luz de Jesus Gallery is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 1986 by entrepreneur and art collector Billy Shire. Housed inside the Soap Plant/Wacko complex on Hollywood Boulevard, the gallery is credited with helping foster what became known as the Lowbrow or Pop Surrealist movement in California art. Its program favors figurative, narrative painting and unconventional sculpture, with content spanning folk, outsider, religious, and sexually charged themes. The gallery states its mission is to bring underground art and counter-culture to a wider audience, and it also operates an Art Advisor Service connecting collectors, curators, and designers with contemporary artists worldwide.

venues.name: Craft Contemporary
venues.about: Craft Contemporary is a nonprofit museum in Los Angeles dedicated to contemporary art made from craft media and processes. It traces its roots to The Egg and the Eye, a restaurant-gallery opened in 1965 by painter Edith Robinson Wyle, which gained nonprofit museum status in 1973 as the Craft & Folk Art Museum. Renamed Craft Contemporary in 2018, the institution presents exhibitions by established and emerging artists and designers often underrepresented in larger art institutions, paired with hands-on workshops and public programs. Located on Wilshire Boulevard's Museum Row, it continues a decades-long tradition of using craft to engage Los Angeles communities through exhibitions, festivals, and educational initiatives.

venues.name: ATLA
venues.about: ATLA is a contemporary gallery in Los Angeles focused on craft-based work, particularly ceramics, that brings together East and West artistic traditions. Its program explores themes of intersectionality, history, heritage, politics, and identity through skilled making. The gallery's name references the Japanese word 'atara,' evoking the sorrow of losing something beautiful, and reflects ATLA's commitment to celebrating endurance and resisting disposability of work, experience, and attention. The gallery operates from a space on Kenmore Avenue and presents exhibitions featuring a wide roster of ceramic and multidisciplinary artists.

venues.name: FOYER-LA
venues.about: FOYER-LA is an artist-run exhibition space in Los Angeles, founded in 2019 by artist Connie Walsh. Set behind a courtyard in front of Walsh's own studio, it describes itself as an in-between space for experimentation, dialogue, and collaboration. Since opening, the gallery has presented more than thirty projects, ranging from solo debuts to conceptually driven installations across sculpture, drawing, and performance. Its program has included artists such as Ellie Krakow, Michael Ashkin, Ana Maria Devis, and James Rose, alongside Walsh's own work. The space favors small-scale, provocative shows that explore themes of intimacy, transition, and the body, positioning itself as a laboratory for experimentation rather than a conventional commercial gallery.

venues.name: Sage Culture
venues.about: Sage Culture is an art gallery and multidisciplinary project space in the Arts District of Los Angeles, founded in 2017 by Nicolas Alonso and Marina Figueiredo. The gallery's concept grew out of a trip to Easter Island and centers on the relationship between people and nature, drawing on ancient and primitive forms of artistic expression. Its program represents artists whose work is deeply tied to natural materials, processes, and themes, spanning ceramics, textiles, photography, and mixed media. Works often blur boundaries between art, craft, and design, emphasizing process, material experimentation, and a meditative or ecological sensibility. The gallery operates by appointment only from its DTLA location.

venues.name: MOCA Grand Avenue
venues.about: MOCA, founded in 1979, is Los Angeles's leading museum dedicated to contemporary art, built around a collection of nearly 8,000 works with deep holdings in LA-based practice alongside international art. MOCA Grand Avenue, the museum's original and flagship site in downtown LA, was designed by architect Arata Isozaki in the 1980s and opened as his first completed US project, announcing MOCA as a major architectural presence on Bunker Hill. The museum also operates The Geffen Contemporary at MOCA, a renovated warehouse in Little Tokyo, and stewards Michael Heizer's land-art work Double Negative in Nevada. Programming spans monographic and thematic exhibitions, education initiatives, publishing, and new-media engagement.

venues.name: Fernberger
venues.about: Fernberger is a Los Angeles gallery founded by Emma Fernberger in January 2024. Located on North Western Avenue, it presents an intergenerational program of artists with a global outlook, placing particular emphasis on women-identifying practitioners. The program is unified by a sense of intensity and immediacy, favoring work that produces an instant visceral reaction while remaining thoughtful and historically grounded. Fernberger has described an interest in art's transformative and unifying potential, seeking pieces that are high-impact yet cerebral. The gallery has participated in major art fairs and been the subject of coverage in international publications, reflecting a growing profile within the Los Angeles gallery scene, particularly around the Melrose Hill area.

venues.name: Marta
venues.about: Marta is a Los Angeles-based, globally-engaged gallery founded in 2019. Its program centers on the space between art and design, giving artists room to experiment with utility and designers room to explore the abandonment of function. Beyond exhibitions, Marta runs curatorial, publication, and podcast initiatives that emphasize the process behind a work's creation as well as the story of its maker. The gallery describes itself as interested in the intersection of disciplines and in advocating for diversity in design and broader public access to the arts. It operates from a space on West Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles.

venues.name: Monte Vista Projects
venues.about: Monte Vista Projects is a Los Angeles artist-run collective founded in 2007. Operating from a fifth-floor space on Maple Avenue downtown, it presents exhibitions, lectures, events, and performances that question standards set by academia and mainstream contemporary art institutions. The collective prioritizes under-represented artists and regularly partners with local, national, and international artist-run spaces, including collaborations and exchanges with groups in Rotterdam, Berlin, and across Southern California. Monte Vista Projects is run collectively by a rotating roster of member-artists who organize its programming, and it maintains an open internship and volunteer program supporting exhibitions, gallery hosting, and installation.

venues.name: John Doe Gallery
venues.about: John Doe Gallery is a Los Angeles space built around a DIY ethos, aiming to foster community and give a platform to emerging artists and new ideas. The gallery presents a small roster whose work spans varied media, from minimalist to mixed-medium practices, and positions itself as a venue for dialogue that pushes against conventional boundaries in contemporary art. It is located on 11th Street in downtown Los Angeles and represents a handful of artists whose profiles are featured on its site, emphasizing versatility and unconventional approaches over any single stylistic or historical focus.

venues.name: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
venues.about: LACMA is the largest art museum in the western United States, holding some 155,000 objects spanning 6,000 years of global art history. It traces its roots to the Los Angeles County Museum of History, Science, and Art (1910) and became an independent institution in 1961, opening on Wilshire Boulevard in 1965. The campus has grown through additions including the Anderson/Art of the Americas Building, the Pavilion for Japanese Art, BCAM, and the Resnick Pavilion, culminating in the 2026 opening of the Peter Zumthor-designed David Geffen Galleries. Located on Wilshire Boulevard in the Miracle Mile, LACMA presents rotating exhibitions across its global collection alongside public programs, education initiatives, and community partnerships, including a gallery at Charles White Elementary School.

venues.name: JAPAN HOUSE Los Angeles
venues.about: JAPAN HOUSE Los Angeles is a cultural institution rather than a commercial gallery, part of a worldwide project with hubs in London, Los Angeles, and São Paulo conceived by Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Located on two floors of Ovation Hollywood, it includes an exhibition gallery, a WAZA Shop, a library, a multi-purpose event hall (Salon), and a restaurant space. Its programming spans Japanese culture broadly, from traditional crafts and regional artisans to contemporary design, food, film, and music, featuring Japanese artists, chefs, and designers alongside professionals influenced by Japan. The organization began operations in Los Angeles starting in 2016, with the venue's grand opening in 2018.

venues.name: Q Pop Shop
venues.about: Q Pop is a small shop and gallery in the historic Little Tokyo district of downtown Los Angeles, opened on November 12, 2010 by co-owners Chris Mitchell, an animation production designer, and Miki Panteepo, a former model turned businesswoman. The shop specializes in curated artist-made goods, vinyl toys, rare records, and designer T-shirts, and is the exclusive West Coast seller of Japanese artist Konatsu.
