Alongside retail, Q Pop houses a mini gallery space that regularly hosts exhibitions, events, and performances featuring illustration and animation talent from studios such as Disney, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, Sony, Warner Brothers, and Netflix.

venues.name: Mek Contemporary
venues.about: Mek Contemporary is a Los Angeles–based gallery presenting contemporary artists working across disciplines and geographies. The program pays particular attention to work engaging memory, migration, displacement, place, identity, and cultural inheritance, favoring artists with distinctive approaches to form, material, and image. The gallery emphasizes close attention to each artist and body of work, developing focused exhibitions and publications alongside sustained relationships with artists, collectors, institutions, and audiences. Through this approach, Mek aims to extend conversations sparked by the work beyond the exhibition space itself, treating each show as part of an ongoing dialogue rather than an isolated event.

venues.name: Formed For + Brodin Gallery
venues.about: Brodin is the shared studio of Los Angeles and UK–based sculptors Gavin and Kelley Brodin, a collaborative artist duo rather than a commercial gallery representing other artists. Working across bronze, stainless steel, stone, and mixed media, they produce monumental public sculpture, private commissions, and immersive installations that explore material transformation, memory, and the tension between the engineered and organic. Their practice spans public art, architectural collaborations, and gallery exhibitions across the United States and internationally, with commissions and installations in cities including Los Angeles, New York, Miami, Mexico City, Tokyo, and Dubai. The site presents no gallery roster, directors, or founding date beyond the artists' own biographical and exhibition history.

venues.name: Cevera Yoon Gallery
venues.about: Cevera Yoon Gallery is a contemporary art space in Los Angeles, founded in 2024 by Kyle Slevira and Green Yoon. Located within the historic Granada building in Koreatown, the gallery occupies over 1,100 square feet across multiple showrooms. Its program is dedicated to presenting both established and emerging artists, offering a platform for innovative and experimental work. The gallery has also participated in art fairs, presenting group exhibitions that explore abstraction across painting and sculpture, engaging with themes of materiality, structure, and the tension between order and entropy in contemporary art practice.

venues.name: Pauhaus Art Gallery + Events
venues.about: Pauhaus Gallery + Events is an artist-founded creative hub on Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles, established in 2021 by artist Pau (Pau Aguirre) after she found a vacant storefront space. What began as the twice-weekly Melrose Drawing Club figure-drawing sessions grew into a multidisciplinary venue hosting exhibitions, comedy shows, open mics, and other community-driven events. The gallery serves as a gathering place for artists, musicians, comedians, and creatives of all kinds, reflecting founder Pau's own background as a muralist and figure-drawing enthusiast. Pauhaus has also been the subject of press coverage for exhibitions of animation and stop-motion artists, and its founder is now exploring expansion of the concept to other cities.

venues.name: Dominique Porter Gallery
venues.about: Dominique Porter Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles presenting emerging and mid-career artists working across painting, sculpture, and installation. Established in 2026, the gallery supports practices marked by sustained material exploration, formal invention, and individual vision. Its program is built around exhibitions, projects, and collaborations intended to give artists room to develop ambitious work and to engage in dialogue with one another and with wider cultural conversations. The gallery describes its approach as artist-centered, bringing together a range of practices while keeping exhibition-making thoughtful and considered rather than driven by a single house style.

venues.name: Korean Cultural Center Los Angeles (KCCLA)
venues.about: The Korean Cultural Center Los Angeles (KCCLA) is a public cultural institution operated by the Republic of Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, located in the Miracle Mile district at 5505 Wilshire Blvd. It functions as a hub for Korean heritage and contemporary culture in the United States, housing a library, a permanent heritage exhibition hall, a second-floor art gallery, an auditorium (Ari Hall), and a media arts wall. Programming spans traditional and contemporary Korean art exhibitions, film screenings, Korean-language classes, and community-oriented shows organized with Korean-American arts associations, alongside field trips and cultural workshops for schools and the public.

venues.name: MAK Center for Art and Architecture — Mackey Apartments
Barnsdall Junior Arts Center Gallery
venues.about: Barnsdall Junior Arts Center (BJAC) Gallery is a public exhibition space within Barnsdall Art Park, operated by the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs (DCA). It is part of a cluster of facilities that also includes the Barnsdall Arts Center (BAC) and the Junior Arts Center itself, all located at 4814 Hollywood Blvd. in Los Angeles. As a civic institution, the gallery's programming is guided by DCA's values framework emphasizing inclusion, diversity, equity, excellence, and access, aiming to deliver arts and cultural programming as a public service to residents and visitors of Los Angeles.

venues.name: Feminist Center for Creative Work
venues.about: The Feminist Center for Creative Work is a non-profit arts and community organization in Los Angeles centered on feminist creative practices. It runs an ongoing program of exhibitions, artist residencies, workshops, and publications intended to foster an intersectional feminist future. Recent programming includes group exhibitions such as Radical Kinship, curated by Chloë Flores, and artist-in-residence projects such as K. Bradford's Wild Glitch. The organization connects visitors to events, groups, and creative work through its website and space, though specific founding details and staff leadership are not stated on the available pages.

venues.name: Grand Central Art Center
venues.about: Grand Central Art Center is a contemporary art space in Santa Ana, California, operated as an outgrowth of California State University, Fullerton. Directed by Chief Curator John Spiak, the center is dedicated to the engaged exploration of contemporary art and visual culture. Its program centers on an active artist-in-residence initiative that supports socially and community-engaged practices, pairing visiting artists with local collaborators, students, and neighborhood residents on long-term projects. Past residencies have ranged from community garden initiatives in nearby housing complexes to a serial broadcast opera staged with regional partners. The center presents resulting exhibitions, public programs, and multimedia projects, and its residency work has drawn coverage from national and regional press outlets.

venues.name: Heavy Manners Library
venues.about: Heavy Manners Library is a lending library, gallery, and bookstore focused on artist-made and independently published media. It offers an alternative to costly formal art education by making self-published books, zines, and other overlooked or out-of-print materials accessible to the public. Members can borrow items with a library card, while visitors may browse the collection during open hours. Alongside its lending program, Heavy Manners hosts events and exhibitions in its gallery, theater, and classroom spaces, aiming to give emerging artists opportunities to share work and established artists room to experiment, with an emphasis on community-oriented educational programming.
